text: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority to make a final decision, provided that it is not amended so that it varies with City policy or by-laws. Transportation Services staff have reviewed the need for traffic calming on Vanauley Street, between Queen Street West and Paul Lane Gardens, to address residents' concerns regarding the speed of vehicles. Our assessment indicates the criteria as set out in the traffic calming policy has not been satisfied. Therefore, traffic calming should not be installed on Vanauley Street, between Queen Street West and Paul Lane Gardens.

The Toronto and East York Community Council directed: 1. The Acting Director of Transportation Services, Toronto and East York District to request the City Clerk to poll eligible householders on Vanauley Street, between Queen Street West and Paul Lane Gardens, to determine whether residents support the installation of traffic calming, in accordance with the City of Toronto Traffic Calming Policy. 2. Subject to favourable results of the poll, the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter the roadway on Vanauley Street, between Queen Street West and Paul Lane Gardens, for traffic calming purposes, generally as shown on the copy of Drawing No. 421G-2950, dated April 2018, attached to the report (March 26, 2018) from the Acting Director, Transportation Services, Toronto and East York District.
